Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Meanwhile, as the operations against Áhmedábád made no progress, Pándurang _____ made offers of peace
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Momín Khán prepared to oppose him, but the Pandit made friendly overtures, and eventually Momín Khán not only paid the sum of Rupees 7000 for grass and grain for the Pandit's troops, but also lent him four small cannon. Pándurang Pandit then marched upon Áhmedábád, and encamping near the Kankaria Lake laid siege to the city which was defended by Jawán Mard Khán.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: About this time the _____ released Dámáji Gáikwár on his promise to help the Peshwa's brother Raghunáthráv, who was shortly afterwards despatched with an army to complete the conquest of Gujarát
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: About this time the Peshwa released Dámáji Gáikwár on his promise to help the Peshwa's brother Raghunáthráv, who was shortly afterwards despatched with an army to complete the conquest of Gujarát.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Meanwhile, Jawán _____án's anxiety regarding the Maráthás was for a time removed by the departure of Pándurang Pandit
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: These Jawán Mard Khán accepted, and on receiving from Jawán Mard Khán the present of a mare and a small sum of money under the name of entertainment, the Marátha leader withdrew to Sorath. Meanwhile, Jawán Mard Khán's anxiety regarding the Maráthás was for a time removed by the departure of Pándurang Pandit.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Jawán _____án then marched from the city, levying tribute until he arrived on the Pálanpur frontier about seventy-five miles north of Áhmedábád
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Certain well informed persons, who had heard of Raghunáthráv's preparations for invading Gujarát, begged Jawán Mard Khán not to leave the city but to depute his brother Zoráwar Khán Bábi to collect the tribute. Jawán Mard Khán, not believing their reports, said that he would not go more than from forty-five to sixty miles from the city, and that, should the necessity of any more distant excursion arise, he would entrust it to his brother.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Here meeting Muhammad Bahádur Jhálori, the governor of Palanpur, Jawán Mard Khán was foolishly induced to join him in plundering the fertile districts of Sirohi, till at last he was not less than ____
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Here meeting Muhammad Bahádur Jhálori, the governor of Palanpur, Jawán Mard Khán was foolishly induced to join him in plundering the fertile districts of Sirohi, till at last he was not less than 150 miles from his headquarters.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Meanwhile, _____áthráv, joining Dámáji Gáikwár, entered suddenly by an unusual route into Gujarát, and news reached Áhmedábád that the Maráthás had crossed the Narmada River
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Meanwhile, Raghunáthráv, joining Dámáji Gáikwár, entered suddenly by an unusual route into Gujarát, and news reached Áhmedábád that the Maráthás had crossed the Narmada River. Raghunáthráv, hearing that Jawán Mard Khán and his army were absent from the city, pressed on by forced marches, and crossing the Mahi River despatched an advance co.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Kosáji, proprietor of _____, at Dámáji Gáikwár's invitation also marched towards Áhmedábád, plundering Mehmúdábád Khokhri, only three miles from the city
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Kosáji, proprietor of Nadiad, at Dámáji Gáikwár's invitation also marched towards Áhmedábád, plundering Mehmúdábád Khokhri, only three miles from the city.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: In the meantime _____ reached Kaira (Kheda), and taking with him the chief man of that place, Muhammad Daurán, son of Muhammad Bábi, continued his march
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Raghunáthráv, hearing that Jawán Mard Khán and his army were absent from the city, pressed on by forced marches, and crossing the Mahi River despatched an advance corps under Vithal Sukhdev. In the meantime Vithal Sukhdev reached Kaira (Kheda), and taking with him the chief man of that place, Muhammad Daurán, son of Muhammad Bábi, continued his march.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: He was shortly joined by _____áthráv, and the combined forces now proceeded to Áhmedábád and encamped by the Kánkaria lake
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Raghunáthráv, hearing that Jawán Mard Khán and his army were absent from the city, pressed on by forced marches, and crossing the Mahi River despatched an advance corps under Vithal Sukhdev. He was shortly joined by Raghunáthráv, and the combined forces now proceeded to Áhmedábád and encamped by the Kánkaria lake.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Next day _____áthráv moved his camp to near the tomb of Sháh Bhíkan, on the bank of the Sabarmati River to the south-west of the city
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: He was shortly joined by Raghunáthráv, and the combined forces now proceeded to Áhmedábád and encamped by the Kánkaria lake. Next day Raghunáthráv moved his camp to near the tomb of Sháh Bhíkan, on the bank of the Sabarmati River to the south-west of the city.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: After leaving Sirohi, Jawán _____án had gone westwards to Tharad and Vav, so that the first messengers failed to find him
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: After leaving Sirohi, Jawán Mard Khán had gone westwards to Tharad and Vav, so that the first messengers failed to find him. One of the later messengers, Mándan by name, who had not left Áhmedábád until the arrival of Raghunáthráv at the Kánkaria lake, made his way to Váv and Tharád, and told Jawán Mard Khán what had happened.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: The presence of Jawán _____án raised the spirits of the besieged, and the defence was conducted with ardour
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: After leaving Sirohi, Jawán Mard Khán had gone westwards to Tharad and Vav, so that the first messengers failed to find him. One of the later messengers, Mándan by name, who had not left Áhmedábád until the arrival of Raghunáthráv at the Kánkaria lake, made his way to Váv and Tharád, and told Jawán Mard Khán what had happened.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: At length, embarrassed by want of provisions and the clamour of his troops for pay, he extorted _____ 50,000 from the official classes
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: At length, embarrassed by want of provisions and the clamour of his troops for pay, he extorted Rupees 50,000 from the official classes.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: At last to _____áthráv's relief, Jawán Mard Khán was reduced to treat for peace through Vithal Sukhdev
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: The official classes who were the repository of all real power murmured against his rule and openly advocated the surrender of the city, and Jawán Mard Khán, much against his will, was forced to enter into negotiations with Raghunáthráv. Raghunáthráv was so little hopeful of taking Áhmedábád that he had determined, should the siege last a month longer, to depart on condition of receiving the one-fourth share of the revenue and a safe conduct.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: It was arranged that the Maráthás should give Jawán _____án the sum of Rupees 1 lákh to pay his troops, besides presenting him with an elephant and other articles of value
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Had Jawán Mard Khán only disbursed his own money to pay the troops, and encouraged instead of disheartening the official class, he need never have lost the city. At last to Raghunáthráv's relief, Jawán Mard Khán was reduced to treat for peace through Vithal Sukhdev.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: It was further agreed that one of Jawán _____án's brothers should always serve the Maráthás with 300 horse and 500 foot, the expenses of the force being paid by the Maráthás
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: It was arranged that the Maráthás should give Jawán Mard Khán the sum of Rupees 1 lákh to pay his troops, besides presenting him with an elephant and other articles of value. And that, for himself and his brothers, Jawán Mard Khán should receive, free from any Marátha claim, the districts of Patan, Vadnagar, Sami, Munjpur, Visnagar, Tharád, Kheralu, and Rádhanpur with Tervada and Vijapur.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: The treaty was then delivered to Jawán Mard Khán, and he and his garrison, marching out with the honours of war, the Maráthás took possession of Áhmedábád on 2 April _____
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: The treaty was then delivered to Jawán Mard Khán, and he and his garrison, marching out with the honours of war, the Maráthás took possession of Áhmedábád on 2 April 1753.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: On leaving Áhmedábád Jawán _____án retired to Pátan
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: The treaty was then delivered to Jawán Mard Khán, and he and his garrison, marching out with the honours of war, the Maráthás took possession of Áhmedábád on 2 April 1753. On leaving Áhmedábád Jawán Mard Khán retired to Pátan.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: At Áhmedábád _____áthráv with Dámáji arranged for the government of the city, appointing Shripatráv his deputy
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: This agreement was signed and sealed by Raghunáthráv, with Dámáji Gáikwár (half sharer), Malhárráv Holkar, Jye Ápa Sindhia, Rámchandar Vithal Sukhdev, Sakhárám Bhagvant, and Mádhavráv Gopálráv as securities. At Áhmedábád Raghunáthráv with Dámáji arranged for the government of the city, appointing Shripatráv his deputy.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: He then marched into _____ to levy tribute from the Limbdi and Wadhwan chiefs; and was so far successful that Harbhamji of Limbḍi agreed to pay an annual tribute of Rupees 40,000
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: He then marched into Jhalawad to levy tribute from the Limbdi and Wadhwan chiefs; and was so far successful that Harbhamji of Limbḍi agreed to pay an annual tribute of Rupees 40,000.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: As the rainy season was drawing near Raghunáthráv returned to Dholka, while _____ forced Muhammad Bahádur, the governor of Palanpur, to consent to a payment of Rupees 1,15,000
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: As the rainy season was drawing near Raghunáthráv returned to Dholka, while Patel Vithal Sukhdev forced Muhammad Bahádur, the governor of Palanpur, to consent to a payment of Rupees 1,15,000.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: From Dholka, _____áthráv went to Tárápur, about twelve miles north of Cambay (Khambhat), and compelled Momín Khán to submit to an annual payment of Rupees 10,000
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: At Áhmedábád Raghunáthráv with Dámáji arranged for the government of the city, appointing Shripatráv his deputy. As the rainy season was drawing near Raghunáthráv returned to Dholka, while Patel Vithal Sukhdev forced Muhammad Bahádur, the governor of Palanpur, to consent to a payment of Rupees 1,15,000.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Dámáji Gáikwár, after levying tribute in the Vátrak Kántha, went to _____, which he took from Sher Khán Bábi
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Dámáji Gáikwár, after levying tribute in the Vátrak Kántha, went to Kapadvanj, which he took from Sher Khán Bábi. From Kapadvanj he passed to Naḍiád and appointed Shevakrái to collect his half share of the revenue of Gujarát.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: From Kapadvanj he passed to Naḍiád and appointed _____ái to collect his half share of the revenue of Gujarát
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: From Kapadvanj he passed to Naḍiád and appointed Shevakrái to collect his half share of the revenue of Gujarát.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Though the imperial power was sunk so low, the emperor was allowed to confer the post of Kázi of the city on Kázi Rûkn-ul-_____án who arrived at Áhmedábád and assumed office
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Though the imperial power was sunk so low, the emperor was allowed to confer the post of Kázi of the city on Kázi Rûkn-ul-Hak Khán who arrived at Áhmedábád and assumed office.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Failure of an Attempt on Cambay, _____ At the close of the year Shripatráv, who was anxious to acquire Cambay, marched against Momín Khán
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Failure of an Attempt on Cambay, 1753 At the close of the year Shripatráv, who was anxious to acquire Cambay, marched against Momín Khán.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: After two doubtful battles in which the Maráthás gained no advantage, it was agreed that Momín Khán should pay a sum of Rupees 7000, and Shripatráv departed from Áhmedábád early in _____
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: After the rains were over (1754) Shetuji, commander of the Áhmedábád garrison, and Shankarji, governor of Víramgám, were sent to collect tribute from Sorath. After two doubtful battles in which the Maráthás gained no advantage, it was agreed that Momín Khán should pay a sum of Rupees 7000, and Shripatráv departed from Áhmedábád early in 1754.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: When the Kolis heard of the ill success of the Maráthás at _____, they revolted and Rághoshankar was sent to subdue them
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Failure of an Attempt on Cambay, 1753 At the close of the year Shripatráv, who was anxious to acquire Cambay, marched against Momín Khán. When the Kolis heard of the ill success of the Maráthás at Cambay, they revolted and Rághoshankar was sent to subdue them.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: In an engagement near Luhára in _____ in the Gáikwár's territory about eighteen miles east of Áhmedábád, Rághoshankar scattered the Kolis, but they again collected and forced the Maráthás to retire
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: In an engagement near Luhára in Bahyal in the Gáikwár's territory about eighteen miles east of Áhmedábád, Rághoshankar scattered the Kolis, but they again collected and forced the Maráthás to retire.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: At this time _____ and Shankarji returned from Sorath, where they had performed the pilgrimage to Dwarka
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: At this time Shetuji and Shankarji returned from Sorath, where they had performed the pilgrimage to Dwarka. Shetuji was sent to the Bhíl district against the Kolis.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Shetuji was sent to the Bhíl district against the _____
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: When the Kolis heard of the ill success of the Maráthás at Cambay, they revolted and Rághoshankar was sent to subdue them. In an engagement near Luhára in Bahyal in the Gáikwár's territory about eighteen miles east of Áhmedábád, Rághoshankar scattered the Kolis, but they again collected and forced the Maráthás to retire.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: He was unsuccessful, and was so ashamed of his failure that he returned to the _____ and Dandu Dátátri was appointed in his place
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: He was unsuccessful, and was so ashamed of his failure that he returned to the Dakhan and Dandu Dátátri was appointed in his place.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: In this year died Nek Álam Khán II, governor of _____
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: In this year died Nek Álam Khán II, governor of Broach.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: He was succeeded by his brother _____án who expelled his nephew Hámid Beg, son of Nek Álam Khán
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: He was succeeded by his brother Khertalab Khán who expelled his nephew Hámid Beg, son of Nek Álam Khán.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Hámid Beg took refuge in _____
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Hámid Beg took refuge in Surat.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: At Bálásinor a dispute arose between _____án Bábi and a body of Arab mercenaries who took possession of a hill, but in the end came to terms
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: At Bálásinor a dispute arose between Sher Khán Bábi and a body of Arab mercenaries who took possession of a hill, but in the end came to terms.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Maráthás Attack Cambay, _____ With the Peshwa's permission his deputy Bhagvantráv marched on Cambay
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Maráthás Attack Cambay, 1754 With the Peshwa's permission his deputy Bhagvantráv marched on Cambay.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Subsequently, a letter from _____áv to Sálim Jamádár at Áhmedábád ordering him to march against Cambay fell into Momín Khán's hands
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Maráthás Attack Cambay, 1754 With the Peshwa's permission his deputy Bhagvantráv marched on Cambay. When Bhagvantráv arrived at Cambay he showed no hostile intentions and was well received by Momín Khán.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: He at once surrounded _____áv's house and made him prisoner
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: When Bhagvantráv arrived at Cambay he showed no hostile intentions and was well received by Momín Khán. Subsequently, a letter from Bhagvantráv to Sálim Jamádár at Áhmedábád ordering him to march against Cambay fell into Momín Khán's hands.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: When the Peshwa heard that _____áv had been captured, he ordered Ganesh Ápa, governor of Jambusar, as well as the governors of Víramgám, Dhandhuka, and other places to march at once upon Cambay
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: When Bhagvantráv arrived at Cambay he showed no hostile intentions and was well received by Momín Khán. Subsequently, a letter from Bhagvantráv to Sálim Jamádár at Áhmedábád ordering him to march against Cambay fell into Momín Khán's hands.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Shortly afterwards _____áv was recalled by the Peshwa and his place supplied by an officer of the name of Rágho
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: Eventually Shripatráv, the Peshwa's deputy, sent the author of the Mirăt-i-Áhmedi to negotiate, and it was agreed that Bhagvantráv should be released and that no alteration should be made in the position of Momín Khán. Shortly afterwards Shripatráv was recalled by the Peshwa and his place supplied by an officer of the name of Rágho.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: About this time _____án, governor of Broach, died, and quarrels arose regarding the succession
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: About this time Khertalab Khán, governor of Broach, died, and quarrels arose regarding the succession. Ultimately Hamid Beg, nephew of Khertalab Khán, obtained the post, and he afterwards received an imperial order confirming him as governor, and bestowing on him the title of Neknám Khán Bahádur.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: Ultimately Hamid Beg, nephew of _____án, obtained the post, and he afterwards received an imperial order confirming him as governor, and bestowing on him the title of Neknám Khán Bahádur
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: About this time Khertalab Khán, governor of Broach, died, and quarrels arose regarding the succession. Ultimately Hamid Beg, nephew of Khertalab Khán, obtained the post, and he afterwards received an imperial order confirming him as governor, and bestowing on him the title of Neknám Khán Bahádur.

Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.question: At Delhi, during _____, the emperor Ahmad Shah Bahadur was deposed, and Âzíz-ud-dín, son of Jahándár Sháh, was raised to the throne with the title of Alamgir II
Gujarat under Ahmad Shah Bahadur.fact: At Delhi, during 1754, the emperor Ahmad Shah Bahadur was deposed, and Âzíz-ud-dín, son of Jahándár Sháh, was raised to the throne with the title of Alamgir II.

Third Anglo-Mysore War.question: The _____ was Conflict in India (1790–1792).
Third Anglo-Mysore War.fact: The Third Anglo-Mysore War (1789–1792) was a military conflict in Southern India between the Sultanate of Mysore and the East India Company, Maratha Empire, Kingdom of Travancore and the Nizam of Hyderabad.

Third Anglo-Mysore War.subject: Ancient India
Third Anglo-Mysore War.question: It was the third of four Anglo-_____
Third Anglo-Mysore War.fact: It was the third of four Anglo-Mysore Wars.

Third Anglo-Mysore War.fact: The First Anglo-Mysore War, fought in the 1760s, had ended inconclusively on both sides, with treaty provisions including promises of mutual assistance in future conflicts.

Third Anglo-Mysore War.subject: Ancient India
Third Anglo-Mysore War.question: British failure to support _____ in conflicts with the Maratha Confederacy and other actions supportive of Mysore's enemies led Hyder to develop a dislike for the British
Third Anglo-Mysore War.fact: The Third Anglo-Mysore War (1789–1792) was a military conflict in Southern India between the Sultanate of Mysore and the East India Company, Maratha Empire, Kingdom of Travancore and the Nizam of Hyderabad. It was the third of four Anglo-Mysore Wars.

Third Anglo-Mysore War.subject: Ancient India
Third Anglo-Mysore War.question: After the British took the French-controlled port of Mahé in _____, Hyder, who had been receiving military supplies through that port and had placed it under his protection, opened the Second Anglo-My
Third Anglo-Mysore War.fact: After the British took the French-controlled port of Mahé in 1779, Hyder, who had been receiving military supplies through that port and had placed it under his protection, opened the Second Anglo-Mysore War.

Third Anglo-Mysore War.subject: Ancient India
Third Anglo-Mysore War.question: He refused to free _____ prisoners taken during the war, one of the conditions of the treaty
Third Anglo-Mysore War.fact: After the British took the French-controlled port of Mahé in 1779, Hyder, who had been receiving military supplies through that port and had placed it under his protection, opened the Second Anglo-Mysore War. This war ended with the last British–Indian treaty with an Indian ruler on equal footing, the 1784 Treaty of Mangalore, which restored the status quo ante bellum under terms company officials such as Warren Hastings found extremely unfavourable for the British East India Company.

Third Anglo-Mysore War.subject: Ancient India
Third Anglo-Mysore War.question: British General Charles, 2nd Earl Cornwallis became the Governor-General of Bengal and Commander-in-Chief for the East India Company in _____
Third Anglo-Mysore War.fact: British General Charles, 2nd Earl Cornwallis became the Governor-General of Bengal and Commander-in-Chief for the East India Company in 1786.

Third Anglo-Mysore War.subject: Ancient India
Third Anglo-Mysore War.question: Also, Pitt's "India Act" came into force in _____, which made East India Company subordinated to the British crown, making the Company's power insignificant and marking the rise of direct British impe
Third Anglo-Mysore War.fact: While he formally abrogated agreements with the Marathas and Hyderabad that violated terms of the 1784 treaty, he sought informally to gain their support and that of the Nizam of Hyderabad, or at least their neutrality, in the event of conflict with Mysore. Also, Pitt's "India Act" came into force in 1784, which made East India Company subordinated to the British crown, making the Company's power insignificant and marking the rise of direct British imperial control in India.

Third Anglo-Mysore War.subject: Ancient India
Third Anglo-Mysore War.question: Thus, unlike the earlier wars, where Tipu and his father confronted the _____, Tipu would now be fighting, in effect, against the British Empire
Third Anglo-Mysore War.fact: British General Charles, 2nd Earl Cornwallis became the Governor-General of Bengal and Commander-in-Chief for the East India Company in 1786. Third Anglo-Mysore War.fact: Thus, unlike the earlier wars, where Tipu and his father confronted the Company, Tipu would now be fighting, in effect, against the British Empire. Travancore had been a target of Tipu for acquisition or conquest since the end of the previous war.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In 1723 Rustam Áli Khán and Shujáât Khán were ordered from Delhi to march on Jodhpur, which they captured and plundered, and then returned to Áhmedábád. Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: The emperor accepted this offer, allowing _____ Áli to draw on the Surat treasury to the extent of Rupees 200000
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Rustam Áli, governor of Surat, having succeeded twice or thrice in defeating the Maráthás under Píláji Gáikwár, now offered, in conjunction with his brother Shujáât Khán, that if 20,000 men were placed under their orders, they would march against the Nizám. Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: He promised to Kántáji Kadam Bánde a one-fourth share of the revenue of Gujarát, provided he should be able, in concert with Hámid Khán, to re-conquer the province from Mubáriz-ul-Mulk. Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Shujáât Khán's head was cut off and sent to Safdar Khán Bábi, to be sent to Ibráhím Kúli his son, who was doing duty as commandant at Áhmedábád.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Ibráhím Kúli, son of _____áât Khán, in revenge for his father's death, determined to assassinate Hámid Khán
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Ibráhím Kúli, son of Shujáât Khán, in revenge for his father's death, determined to assassinate Hámid Khán.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Hámid Khán, accompanied by Mír Nathu, _____ábat Rohila, and Kántáji Kadam, marched to oppose Rustam Khán

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Now, as the Maráthás really desired to ruin _____ Áli, who was their bitter foe, they after a few days surrounded him and cut off his supplies

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Under his advice, Salábat _____án Bábi was appointed governor of Víramgám, and Jawán Mard Khán governor of Pátan

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: About this time Áli Muhammad Khán, the father of the author of the Mirăt-i-Áhmedi, who was now with Mubáriz-ul-Mulk at Mehsána, advised him to conciliate the influential family of Bábi. Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk deputed his son Khánahzád Khán with an army to oppose them, and made several appointments, among other changes raising Áli Muhammad Khán to the post of minister.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Defeat of the Maráthás at Sojitra and Kapadvanj, 1725 Khánahzád Khán met the Maráthás near Sojitra, about ten miles north-west of Petlád, and defeated them, pursuing them as far as the Mahi.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Defeat of the Maráthás at Sojitra and Kapadvanj, 1725 Khánahzád Khán met the Maráthás near Sojitra, about ten miles north-west of Petlád, and defeated them, pursuing them as far as the Mahi. Then, returning, he was reinforced by his brother Sháh Nawáz Khán, and marched against the Maráthás, who were encamped at Kapadvanj.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Another battle was fought, and the Maráthás were again defeated and pursued as far as the hills of Áli-Mohan now Chhota Udaipur in the extreme east of the province.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Khánahzád Khán now appointed Hasan-ud-dín governor of Baroda, _____, Jambusar, and Makbulábád
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Khánahzád Khán now appointed Hasan-ud-dín governor of Baroda, Bharuch, Jambusar, and Makbulábád.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: The Nágars accordingly, seeing no prospect of help, paid a sum of _____ 400000 and Antáji Bháskar retired
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The Nágars accordingly, seeing no prospect of help, paid a sum of Rupees 400000 and Antáji Bháskar retired.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Kántáji again laid siege to _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Vadnagar was inhabited by wealthy Bráhmans of the Nágar caste who prayed Mubáriz-ul-Mulk to march to their relief; but as both his sons were in pursuit of the other Marátha bands defeated at Kapadvanj, the viceroy had no troops to spare from the Áhmedábád garrison. Kántáji again laid siege to Vadnagar.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Shortly afterwards Umreth in the Kaira district suffered a similar fate at the hands of Kántáji.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In one of his raids Píláji Gáikwár advancing as far as Baroda was met by Khánahzád Khán, the son of the viceroy.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Distrusting the issue of a battle Píláji fled to Cambay, and from Cambay withdrew to Sorath.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: For these services the emperor raised Khánahzád Khán to the rank of a noble, with the title Ghálib Jang.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Not long afterwards Áli _____án was again entrusted with a command and raised to be governor of Dholka
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: About this time Áli Muhammad Khán was dismissed from the post of minister, and in his stead first Muhammad Sayad Beg and afterwards Muhammad Sulaimán were appointed. Not long afterwards Áli Muhammad Khán was again entrusted with a command and raised to be governor of Dholka.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: The Maráthás retired to the Dakhan, but, returning in _____, compelled Mubáriz-ul-Mulk to confirm his predecessor's grants in their favour
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The Maráthás retired to the Dakhan, but, returning in 1726, compelled Mubáriz-ul-Mulk to confirm his predecessor's grants in their favour.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: As part of the agreement between Mubáriz-ul-_____ and the Marátha chiefs Píláji was to receive a share in the revenue of the districts south of the Mahi
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The Maráthás retired to the Dakhan, but, returning in 1726, compelled Mubáriz-ul-Mulk to confirm his predecessor's grants in their favour. As part of the agreement between Mubáriz-ul-Mulk and the Marátha chiefs Píláji was to receive a share in the revenue of the districts south of the Mahi.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: About this time want of funds forced Mubáriz-ul-Mulk to sell the greater part of the _____ district to different landholders
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: About this time want of funds forced Mubáriz-ul-Mulk to sell the greater part of the Dholka district to different landholders.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Though he did not consent to these proposals, the viceroy so far accepted the alliance of the _____ as to allow the governor of Baroda to aid Udáji Pavár against Píláji
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Kántáji, perceiving that if the Peshwa became supreme his own independence would suffer, joined Píláji, and marching together upon Baroda they endeavoured, but without success, to prevent the Mughal governor Sadr-ud-dín Khán from entering the city. In the following year, 1727, Bájiráv Peshwa began to negotiate with Mubáriz-ul-Mulk, undertaking that if the one-fourth and one-tenth shares in the revenue of the province were guaranteed to him, he would protect Gujarát from other invaders.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Piláji Gáikwár obtains Baroda and Dabhoi, _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In the following year, 1727, Bájiráv Peshwa began to negotiate with Mubáriz-ul-Mulk, undertaking that if the one-fourth and one-tenth shares in the revenue of the province were guaranteed to him, he would protect Gujarát from other invaders. Piláji Gáikwár obtains Baroda and Dabhoi, 1727.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Píláji Gáikwár now obtained possession of _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Though he did not consent to these proposals, the viceroy so far accepted the alliance of the Peshwa as to allow the governor of Baroda to aid Udáji Pavár against Píláji. Piláji Gáikwár obtains Baroda and Dabhoi, 1727.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk, still sorely pressed for funds, marched into _____ to exact tribute
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk, still sorely pressed for funds, marched into Sorath to exact tribute.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: On reaching Víramgám, Salábat _____án Bábi, on behalf of the Jám of Nawánagar, presented the viceroy with Rupees 100000, and for this service was rewarded with the gift of an elephant
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: On reaching Víramgám, Salábat Muhammad Khán Bábi, on behalf of the Jám of Nawánagar, presented the viceroy with Rupees 100000, and for this service was rewarded with the gift of an elephant.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk then marched against Chháya, the capital of the chief of _____ in the south-west of Káthiáwad
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Mubáriz-ul-Mulk then marched against Chháya, the capital of the chief of Porbandar in the south-west of Káthiáwad.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: But on hearing that the viceroy proposed to annex his territory and appoint an officer to govern it, he returned and agreed to pay a tribute of _____ 40,000
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: On reaching Víramgám, Salábat Muhammad Khán Bábi, on behalf of the Jám of Nawánagar, presented the viceroy with Rupees 100000, and for this service was rewarded with the gift of an elephant. But on hearing that the viceroy proposed to annex his territory and appoint an officer to govern it, he returned and agreed to pay a tribute of Rupees 40,000.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: About this time the viceroy received orders from the emperor to restore certain land which he had confiscated, and as he neglected to obey, certain estates of his in the _____áb were resumed
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: About this time the viceroy received orders from the emperor to restore certain land which he had confiscated, and as he neglected to obey, certain estates of his in the Panjáb were resumed.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Capture of Chámpáner by the Maráthás, _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Capture of Chámpáner by the Maráthás, 1728. In 1728 the minister Momín Khán died, and in his place the emperor selected Momín Khán's brother Abd-ul-Ghani Khán.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: In _____ the minister Momín Khán died, and in his place the emperor selected Momín Khán's brother Abd-ul-Ghani Khán
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Capture of Chámpáner by the Maráthás, 1728. In 1728 the minister Momín Khán died, and in his place the emperor selected Momín Khán's brother Abd-ul-Ghani Khán.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: About this time Asad Áli, governor of Junágaḍh, also died, and on his deathbed appointed Salábat _____án Bábi, deputy governor of that fortress
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: About this time Asad Áli, governor of Junágaḍh, also died, and on his deathbed appointed Salábat Muhammad Khán Bábi, deputy governor of that fortress. Salábat Muhammad Khán sent his son Sher Khán Bábi to act on his behalf.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Salábat _____án sent his son Sher Khán Bábi to act on his behalf
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: About this time Asad Áli, governor of Junágaḍh, also died, and on his deathbed appointed Salábat Muhammad Khán Bábi, deputy governor of that fortress. Salábat Muhammad Khán sent his son Sher Khán Bábi to act on his behalf.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: When the emperor heard of the death of _____ Áli, he appointed Ghulám Muhy-ud-dín Khán, son of the late Asad Áli, governor
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: About this time Asad Áli, governor of Junágaḍh, also died, and on his deathbed appointed Salábat Muhammad Khán Bábi, deputy governor of that fortress. When the emperor heard of the death of Asad Áli, he appointed Ghulám Muhy-ud-dín Khán, son of the late Asad Áli, governor.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: The Peshwa accordingly sent his brother _____ájiráv to collect the tribute
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The Peshwa accordingly sent his brother Chimnájiráv to collect the tribute. Chimnáji plundered Dholka and the country near Chámpáner, while Mubáriz-ul-Mulk exacted tribute from the chiefs on the banks of the Vatrak river.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Chimnáji plundered _____ and the country near Chámpáner, while Mubáriz-ul-Mulk exacted tribute from the chiefs on the banks of the Vatrak river
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Chimnáji plundered Dholka and the country near Chámpáner, while Mubáriz-ul-Mulk exacted tribute from the chiefs on the banks of the Vatrak river.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Kántáji now entered _____át and prepared for war in case Chimnáji and the viceroy should unite against him
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Ghulám Muhy-ud-dín did not proceed to Junágaḍh but continued Sher Khán Bábi as his deputy perceiving that neither Píláji nor Kántáji afforded any protection to Gujarát, but rather pillaged it, closed with the offers of Bájiráv Peshwa, and in 1729 formally granted to him the one-fourth and one-tenth shares of the revenue of the province. Kántáji now entered Gujarát and prepared for war in case Chimnáji and the viceroy should unite against him.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: His movements were not interfered with, and after collecting his share of the tribute, he retired to _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: His movements were not interfered with, and after collecting his share of the tribute, he retired to Sorath.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: The viceroy now marched against the Kolis, and after destroying many of them together with their wives and children, returned to Áhmedábád by way of Modasa and _____ (Himatnagar)
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The viceroy now marched against the Kolis, and after destroying many of them together with their wives and children, returned to Áhmedábád by way of Modasa and Ahmednagar (Himatnagar).

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Through the influence of the viceroy this appointment was not confirmed, and instead Sher Khán Bábi, son of Salábat _____án, was placed in charge of that fortress
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Through the influence of the viceroy this appointment was not confirmed, and instead Sher Khán Bábi, son of Salábat Muhammad Khán, was placed in charge of that fortress.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Mulla Muhammad Áli raises a Disturbance at Surat, 1729 In Surat, the year 1729, was marked by a severe flood in the Tapti river and by a somewhat serious local disturbance.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: The chief cause of the disturbance was _____ Áli, a rich Muslim trader of Surat
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Mulla Muhammad Áli raises a Disturbance at Surat, 1729 In Surat, the year 1729, was marked by a severe flood in the Tapti river and by a somewhat serious local disturbance. The chief cause of the disturbance was Mulla Muhammad Áli, a rich Muslim trader of Surat.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: As Píram was not popular, _____ fixed on the village of Athwa, on the left bank of the Tápti, about twelve miles from its mouth
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The chief cause of the disturbance was Mulla Muhammad Áli, a rich Muslim trader of Surat. As Píram was not popular, Mulla Muhammad fixed on the village of Athwa, on the left bank of the Tápti, about twelve miles from its mouth.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Here he began to build a fort, but was ordered to desist by _____áb Khán, the governor of Surat, from which city the proposed stronghold was only three miles distant
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Here he began to build a fort, but was ordered to desist by Sohráb Khán, the governor of Surat, from which city the proposed stronghold was only three miles distant. Accordingly, next day, Beglar-Beg Khán bombarded the governor Sohráb Khán's residence, proclaiming that his own brother Teghbeg Khán was appointed governor of Surat.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Mulla Muhammad so far from obeying, persuaded Beglar-_____án the commander of the fort of Surat to side with him
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Mulla Muhammad so far from obeying, persuaded Beglar-Beg Khán the commander of the fort of Surat to side with him. Accordingly, next day, Beglar-Beg Khán bombarded the governor Sohráb Khán's residence, proclaiming that his own brother Teghbeg Khán was appointed governor of Surat.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Accordingly, next day, _____-Beg Khán bombarded the governor Sohráb Khán's residence, proclaiming that his own brother Teghbeg Khán was appointed governor of Surat
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Mulla Muhammad so far from obeying, persuaded Beglar-Beg Khán the commander of the fort of Surat to side with him. Accordingly, next day, Beglar-Beg Khán bombarded the governor Sohráb Khán's residence, proclaiming that his own brother Teghbeg Khán was appointed governor of Surat.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Naḍiád given in Farm, 1729. In the same year, 1729, Jawán Mard Khán Bábi was chosen governor of Petlad, Áli Muhammad Khán was made collector of Áhmedábád, and Áli Muhammad's son, the author of the Mirăt-i-Áhmedi and his brother were appointed governor and superintendent of the customs of that district.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Áli _____án shortly resigned and was succeeded by Rú-ín Khán
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In the same year, 1729, Jawán Mard Khán Bábi was chosen governor of Petlad, Áli Muhammad Khán was made collector of Áhmedábád, and Áli Muhammad's son, the author of the Mirăt-i-Áhmedi and his brother were appointed governor and superintendent of the customs of that district. Áli Muhammad Khán shortly resigned and was succeeded by Rú-ín Khán.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: On the death of Jawán _____án, at the request of Salábat Muhammad Khán Bábi, his eldest son Kamál-ud-dín Khán Bábi received the districts of Sami and Munjpur and the title of Jawán Mard Khán
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In the same year, 1729, Jawán Mard Khán Bábi was chosen governor of Petlad, Áli Muhammad Khán was made collector of Áhmedábád, and Áli Muhammad's son, the author of the Mirăt-i-Áhmedi and his brother were appointed governor and superintendent of the customs of that district. At this time Jawán Mard Khán Bábi, while punishing the Kolis of Bálor, probably Bhátod about fifteen miles east of Bharuch, was killed by a man of that tribe, and in revenge for his death the town of Bálor was plundered.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: At the same time the second son, _____, with the title of Safdar Khán, was appointed to the government of Radhanpur
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: At the same time the second son, Muhammad Anwar, with the title of Safdar Khán, was appointed to the government of Radhanpur.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: The viceroy now went to Naḍiád, where Rái Kishandás, agent of Jawán _____án, received the district of Petlád in farm
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: At this time Jawán Mard Khán Bábi, while punishing the Kolis of Bálor, probably Bhátod about fifteen miles east of Bharuch, was killed by a man of that tribe, and in revenge for his death the town of Bálor was plundered. On the death of Jawán Mard Khán, at the request of Salábat Muhammad Khán Bábi, his eldest son Kamál-ud-dín Khán Bábi received the districts of Sami and Munjpur and the title of Jawán Mard Khán.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: On his way back to Áhmedábád the viceroy levied tribute from the chief of Umeta, fifteen miles west of _____
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: From Naḍiád, Mubáriz-ul-Mulk went to collect tribute from Sarḍársingh, the chief of Bhadarva in the Rewa Kántha about fifteen miles north of Baroda, on the banks of the Mahi river, who, after some fighting, agreed to pay a sum of Rs. On his way back to Áhmedábád the viceroy levied tribute from the chief of Umeta, fifteen miles west of Baroda.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: As Rái _____ás failed to pay the sum agreed on for the farm of Petlád, an order was issued for his imprisonment
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The viceroy now went to Naḍiád, where Rái Kishandás, agent of Jawán Mard Khán, received the district of Petlád in farm. As Rái Kishandás failed to pay the sum agreed on for the farm of Petlád, an order was issued for his imprisonment.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Athva Fort, _____ When Kántáji returned from Sorath he camped at Sanand, and his advanced guard carried off some of the viceroy's elephants which were grazing there
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Athva Fort, 1730 When Kántáji returned from Sorath he camped at Sanand, and his advanced guard carried off some of the viceroy's elephants which were grazing there.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Meanwhile, at Surat, _____ Áli continued to build the fort at Athva
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Meanwhile, at Surat, Mulla Muhammad Áli continued to build the fort at Athva.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: In spite of this the _____ succeeded in persuading Sohráb Khán to allow him to go on with his fort promising in return to get him confirmed as governor of Surat
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Meanwhile, at Surat, Mulla Muhammad Áli continued to build the fort at Athva. At last his accomplice, Beglar-Beg Khán the commander of the Surat fort, began to perceive that if the Athva fort were completed the Mulla would be in a position to obstruct the trade of the port of Surat.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: As the fort was immediately below _____ the revenue of Surat was greatly diminished, and Sohráb Khán, when it was too late, saw his mistake
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: In spite of this the Mulla succeeded in persuading Sohráb Khán to allow him to go on with his fort promising in return to get him confirmed as governor of Surat. As the fort was immediately below Surat the revenue of Surat was greatly diminished, and Sohráb Khán, when it was too late, saw his mistake.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: The Viceroy in Káthiáváḍa and Kutch, _____ In 1730, Mubáriz-ul-Mulk went into Gohilwad in south-east Kathiawad and levied tribute from Bhávsingh, chief of Sihor; then he proceeded to Mádhupur, a town
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The Viceroy in Káthiáváḍa and Kutch, 1730 In 1730, Mubáriz-ul-Mulk went into Gohilwad in south-east Kathiawad and levied tribute from Bhávsingh, chief of Sihor; then he proceeded to Mádhupur, a town under Porbandar, and laid it waste.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: The viceroy now marched in the direction of _____ and refusing the offer of a yearly tribute of about 10,00,000 mahmúdis, advanced against Bhuj
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The Viceroy in Káthiáváḍa and Kutch, 1730 In 1730, Mubáriz-ul-Mulk went into Gohilwad in south-east Kathiawad and levied tribute from Bhávsingh, chief of Sihor; then he proceeded to Mádhupur, a town under Porbandar, and laid it waste. The viceroy now marched in the direction of Kutch and refusing the offer of a yearly tribute of about 10,00,000 mahmúdis, advanced against Bhuj.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Riots at Áhmedábád The author of the Mirăt-i-Áhmedi was ordered to suppress the Áhmedábád riots, which had arisen out of the levy of some fresh taxes, and was invested with the title of _____án
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Riots at Áhmedábád The author of the Mirăt-i-Áhmedi was ordered to suppress the Áhmedábád riots, which had arisen out of the levy of some fresh taxes, and was invested with the title of Hasan Muhammad Khán.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: The friends of order endeavoured to arrange a peaceable transfer between the Mahárája and the late viceroy, but Mubáriz-ul-Mulk determined to try the chances of war, and prepared for resistance.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: At this time Mír Ismáíl, deputy of Ghulám Muhy-ud-dín Khán, arrived and took charge of the government of Junágaḍh from _____án Bábi
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: At this time Mír Ismáíl, deputy of Ghulám Muhy-ud-dín Khán, arrived and took charge of the government of Junágaḍh from Sher Khán Bábi.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: Mahárája _____, after making various appointments, set out with his brother Vakhatsingh and 20,000 men to take over the government of Gujarát
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Mahárája Abheysingh, after making various appointments, set out with his brother Vakhatsingh and 20,000 men to take over the government of Gujarát.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: When the Mahárája reached _____ he was joined by Safdar Khán Bábi and Jawán Mard Khán Bábi from Radhanpur
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: When the Mahárája reached Sidhpur he was joined by Safdar Khán Bábi and Jawán Mard Khán Bábi from Radhanpur.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: They then advanced together to Adalaj, distant only about eight miles from _____, their army increasing daily
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: They then advanced together to Adalaj, distant only about eight miles from Ahmedabad, their army increasing daily.

Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.question: But as both Mubáriz-ul-_____ and the Mahárája fought disguised as common soldiers, neither party succeeded
Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.fact: Battle of Adálaj (1730) and Mubáriz-ul-Mulk defeated Mubáriz-ul-Mulk was already encamped between Adálaj and the city, and on the approach of the Mahárája a battle was fought in which the Mahárája was defeated. Gujarat under Muhammad Shah.subject: Ancient India
